title: Ten reds dealt. What comes next?
hook: A full deck, and the first ten cards dealt are all red. Is the next card a coin flip?

knows: coin flips are independent: a run of heads does not make tails due
doesNotKnow: that drawing without putting back breaks independence
how to count what is left in the deck

misconception: Each card is a fresh 50/50 draw, so after ten reds the next card is still 50% red (or black is 'due' for no reason).
objective: The learner can explain that dealt cards are used up, so after ten reds the next card is red 16/42 = 38% of the time, while with replacement (or with coins) it stays 50%.
keyState: Ten reds dealt with 16 red and 26 black left (16 of 42 = 38%), then cards put back (26 of 52 = 50%).

claims.text: A standard deck has 26 red and 26 black cards.
claims.source: Standard 52-card deck: hearts and diamonds red, clubs and spades black.

claims.text: After ten reds are dealt and not put back, 16 red and 26 black remain, so the next card is red 16 times in 42, about 38%.
claims.source: 26 - 10 = 16 red of 52 - 10 = 42; 16/42 = 0.381 (left() in src/demos/probability/cards-do-remember/model.ts). The options 50% / 38% / 62% are pct(1/2), pct(16/42), pct(26/42).

claims.text: Each red dealt lowers the chance the next is red: after one red it is 25 of 51 (49%).
claims.source: left(d, false) = (26 - d)/(52 - d); readout on stage for every d from 0 to 10.

claims.text: If each card is put back and shuffled in, the deck is 26 red of 52 again and the next card is red 50% of the time.
claims.source: Sampling with replacement: left(d, true) = 26/52 for every d.

claims.text: A coin has no pile to run out of, so after any run of flips the next flip is still 50/50. For cards, what changes is the mix of the remaining deck, not any 'due-ness': the next card follows what is left.
claims.source: Independent fair flips: P(next = heads | any past sequence) = 1/2. For cards the dependence is c2. | BUILDER 2026-10-13: stage and claim reworded per fact-check; needs re-verification.

claims.text: The stage forces the first 10 dealt cards to be red; it is a 'suppose this happened' setup, not how often it happens.
claims.source: Stage text 'We make the first 10 cards red'. For reference (not shown): a shuffled deck starts with ten reds C(26,10)/C(52,10) = 0.00034, about 1 in 2,978 (allRedFirst() in model.ts). The brief's figure of 0.0014 was wrong; it is not used.

recall.question: A bag has 5 green and 5 white marbles. You draw 3 greens and keep them out. What is the chance the next marble is green?
recall.why: Three greens are used up: 2 green remain among 7 marbles. Without replacement the bag remembers what left it.
